findings.message: Off by one. The offset is START (`_offset=${_start:-0}`) and the awk prints `NR + offset`. So `-n 120` numbers the first line 121, and the README example does not keep the original line numbers. The default is only right because an unset START maps to 0. Use `offset = START - 1`, with the default being 0 when START is unset. For example, set `_start=1` initially and use `_start - 1`.

`lk_check_files number $@` lost its quotes (it was `"$@"`). Filenames containing spaces or glob characters are now split or expanded, so the check validates the wrong paths. This is a regression unrelated to the feature. Restore `"$@"`.

There are no tests for `-n` in tests/t_number.sh. They should cover `-n 5` starting at 5, `-n 1` and the default, `-n 0`, an invalid value such as `-n x` or `-n -1`, a missing argument, and numbering continuing across multiple files. A test for the start value would have caught the off-by-one. Also, `exit 1` on an invalid start bypasses the shared error helpers that the other option errors use. Check whether the tests/t_conventions.sh exit-code convention expects 2.

pull_request.title: number: add -n START to begin numbering at START
pull_request.body:
Adds `-n START` to `linekit number`, so a numbered excerpt can keep the line numbers of the file it was cut from:

    sed -n 120,140p f | linekit number -n 120

The command table in README.md is updated.
